quote: “On that best portion of a good man’s life; / His little, nameless, unremembered acts / Of kindness and of love.”
source: William Wordsworth, Lines written a few miles above Tintern Abbey, lines 35 to 37, Lyrical Ballads (J. and A. Arch, 1798)
note: Wording verified in the 1798 Lyrical Ballads text. The proposal had the line numbers the wrong way round: counted line by line in the 1798 printing the passage falls at 35 to 37, and the standard later text numbers it 33 to 35.

evidence.where: Project Gutenberg transcription of Lyrical Ballads (1798), ebook 9622, and the Wikisource Lyrical Ballads (1798) page; wording matches exactly, with the semicolon after life and no comma after unremembered.
evidence.edition: Lyrical Ballads, with a Few Other Poems (J. and A. Arch, 1798)
evidence.locator: Lines written a few miles above Tintern Abbey, lines 35 to 37 counted in the 1798 printing (33 to 35 in the standard text)

reason: The three lines are in the 1798 text exactly as proposed, but the proposal misstated the numbering; the line count is corrected and the wording ships as printed in 1798. Not shipped, not near a shipped line, not banned, not at cap.
